title: `ASOF [LEFT] JOIN ... ON eqs AND l.t >= r.t` matches the shape of sverify.asof_join
verdict: no-finding: the join returns a result the as-of shape allows
description: Per left row, the right row of its equality group with the greatest `r.t` at or before `l.t` (`l.t >= r.t`, equal values match). A NULL key or a NULL `t` on either side never matches. LEFT keeps the unmatched left rows with NULLs, INNER drops them. Equal left rows each keep their match: the join returns one row per matched left row. At a tie on `r.t` the result is one of the tied rows, whole (every right column comes from the same row). With no equality there is one group. An empty right side matches nothing; an empty left side gives no rows.

Probed on DATE, TIMESTAMP, INTEGER, BIGINT and VARCHAR `t` and on INTEGER and VARCHAR keys. Doubles are not covered (NaN and the zeros): the writer keeps the range join for them (ruling 162 A3). The strict and mirrored comparisons (`>`, `<=`, `<`) are not covered either: the writer emits `>=` only.
reference: `sverify.asof_join` and the lift of DuckDB's `ASOF JOIN` (`sverify.sql_lift`, #805) write the shape: the left rows numbered, the inner (left) join on the equalities and `NOT(l.t < r.t)`, ranked per left row by `r.t` descending, the first kept. The DuckDB writer emits `ASOF JOIN` for that shape (#1447 item 6); at a tie on `r.t` the pick may differ from the range join's, and the report says `deterministic` is false there.

evidence.observed: [(1, None), (2, None), (3, None), (4, None), (5, None), (6, None), (7, None), (8, None), (9, None)]

SELECT a.t, b.t FROM (SELECT 5::INTEGER AS t) a ASOF LEFT JOIN (SELECT 3::INTEGER AS t) b ON a.t >= b.t
SELECT a.t, b.t FROM (SELECT 'b'::VARCHAR AS t) a ASOF LEFT JOIN (SELECT 'a'::VARCHAR AS t) b ON a.t >= b.t
